newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM not secretly negative to EMU - spokewoman.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM not secretly negative to EMU - spokewoman.

text.p: Sweden's Prime Minister Goran Persson's spokeswoman on Wednesday denied a newspaper report that Persson was more negative to membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) than he pretended to be.

"What Persson says officially and internally tally very well. There are no mixed signals," Persson's spokewoman Ingrid Iremark told Reuters, dismissing the report in daily Svenska Dagbladet as speculation.
The newspaper quoted sources as saying Persson and Finance Minister Erik Asbrink were negative to EMU membership.
A source from the party told the newspaper that the two ministers will not openly admit that they are against a Swedish EMU membership as they fear interest rates will rise.
The party board is due to present its view on EMU in the next few weeks, at the earliest next week, Svenska Dagbladet said.
"The wording will be woolly," a source was quoted as saying.
